fields.why: Table 2 compares male vs female suppression within age groups within countries, and the text claims this held 'across all surveys', a comparison within levels of a third variable; A's reading (series over time by group) is defensible for Table 1 only.
Table 1 change is relative per its footnote, but Table 2 '% Change' values are percentage-point differences (86.1-67.6=18.5), so both scales are computed; A spotted this.
PHIA surveys are nationally representative surveys of six African countries; the brief's national-survey list names only U.S. surveys, so 'national survey' and 'other survey' are both defensible.

Female sex workers and persons who inject drugs appear as HIV key-population categories; by analogy with the MSM rule they are not SPDs unless framed as social position, and the equity framing names MSM, transgender persons and prisoners. A rule on key populations would decide it.

The report evaluates PEPFAR, whose stated core aim is addressing inequities in access, and measures key populations' progress against the UNAIDS 95% target, which meets 'measures progress against a target'; B's 'monitoring only' reading is defensible.

brief_issues: National survey list is U.S.-only (PHIA unclear); no rule for HIV key populations other than MSM; equity_action 'target' clause does not say whether a general program target counts.
